interface.name: bifrost_window_level_manager_v1
interface.description:
Lets the shell put a toplevel on the floating level. A floating window stays above the normal windows of the desktop and is raised only within its own band; menus, panels and the menu bar are not affected. The level belongs to the surface: the window server keeps it for the window's next map too.
Since version 2 the window server also reports where it put each of the client's own toplevels (`frame`): the window server places, moves and resizes toplevels, and a client never learns their position from xdg-shell.
Since version 3 the shell can also ask the window server to place a toplevel (`tile`): the halves, the quarters, fill, centre and the way back to the previous size, the same actions the window server's own Ctrl+Super arrow keys perform. Full screen is the plain xdg_toplevel set_fullscreen and unset_fullscreen.

request.name: set_level

description.summary: set the stacking level of the toplevel of a surface

request.description: Applies at once to a mapped toplevel, and on its next map otherwise.

request.name: tile

description.summary: place the toplevel of a surface

request.description: Places the toplevel of `surface` as `placement` says and configures the client to the new size; the frame comes back in a `frame` event. Ignored for a surface that is not a mapped toplevel of the window server and for a full-screen toplevel.

event.name: frame

description.summary: the window server's frame of a toplevel

event.description: The frame the window server holds for the toplevel of `surface`, in logical desktop pixels: the window geometry the client set (a shadow margin outside it is not part of the frame), so a point at (gx, gy) inside the window geometry is at (x + gx, y + gy) on the desktop. Sent when the toplevel maps, moves or resizes, and for the client's mapped toplevels when it binds. Only toplevels of the binding client are reported; a minimized toplevel is not reported until it is shown again.

entry.name: previous
entry.summary: back to the size before the last fill or tile
